_readme: The existing-project half of drop-in onboarding: what the SessionStart hook offers when a project has source code but no .backend-suite/. It sequences four things that already work when driven by hand — survey, scaffold from the survey, propose mappings, bootstrap docs — so a user does not have to know them. Every step that writes is a checkpoint. init.py is not a skill, so the scaffold is carried as the map-project step's decision point rather than invented as a fake step.
name: understand-existing-project
description: Understand an existing, unconfigured codebase and build its context documentation, one confirmed step at a time.

steps.purpose: Detect the stack, source roots, candidate token sources and document inventory, and list what could not be determined. Writes .backend-suite/survey.json (creating .backend-suite/).
steps.decisionPoint: This creates .backend-suite/survey.json in the project. Confirm before running. If /survey refuses on an unconfigured project, run python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/survey.py" --project-root . directly.
steps.checkpointReason: It is the first write into the project, and the user should read couldNotDetermine before anything is built on it.

steps.purpose: Scaffold .backend-suite/ config seeded from the survey, then propose which document fills each role, the project kind and the true token source — all written as provenance 'inferred'.
steps.decisionPoint: If .backend-suite/profile.json does not exist yet, show the user what python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/init.py" --from-survey --dir . will create, and run it only on their yes. Then run map-project.
steps.checkpointReason: Both halves write config. Inferred mappings are guesses until a human ratifies them with /ratify.

steps.purpose: Reverse-engineer the project's context documents from what is built, proposing each document for accept or decline.
steps.skipIf: The project already has the documents the mapped roles need.
steps.checkpointReason: Writes documents; the skill's own contract is one document at a time with sign-off.

steps.purpose: Propose values for the TODO config sections a code scan can measure (layer rules, adapter seam, animated-widget list, colour token names), each with evidence and _provenance state 'inferred'. Preview by default; writes a section only with --apply.
steps.decisionPoint: Show each proposed section's value and evidence and ask per section. Run --apply only for the sections the user accepted. Exit 2 on the preview means nothing could be inferred — report the reasons and continue.
steps.checkpointReason: Writes .backend-suite/ config that turns refusing audits into running ones; an inferred rule must be confirmed by a human section by section.

steps.purpose: Record where the project starts — which audits are configured, clean, or refusing — now that config exists. Not write-free: every audit leaves a findings envelope under .backend-suite/findings/ (ignored by init's .gitignore), and the raw reports audits save (e.g. .backend-suite/tokens-findings.json) also land inside .backend-suite/, covered by the scaffolded .backend-suite/.gitignore.
steps.checkpointReason: Report-only: it edits no source, config or document, and nothing downstream depends on sign-off. Its regenerable output is named in purpose, which is what chain.py next prints.
